headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: Firecrawl can handle API keys and broad egress while Great Expectations reads files locally, creating a plausible shared-data path but no direct evidence of unsafe defaults.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl can ingest web content and expose it through API/MCP-style surfaces, while Great Expectations consumes files and validation inputs. A prompt-injection bridge is plausible only if Firecrawl output is manually or programmatically fed into Great Expectations as trusted text; no shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this low.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is copied into Great Expectations documentation or test definitions as trusted instructions
IF both agents are connected through a shared file or message channel without content provenance checks
mitigations: Separate raw crawl output from validation config files
Add a manual review step before any Firecrawl-derived text is reused
Store agent outputs in distinct directories
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches API keys and broad web content, and Great Expectations reads data sources and writes validation results. If they share a workspace or files, sensitive inputs can flow from Firecrawl into Great Expectations outputs or logs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default file-based workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem or workspace
IF Firecrawl outputs include API keys, screenshots, or scraped sensitive content that Great Expectations reads or logs
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Redact secrets before handing files to Great Expectations
Restrict Firecrawl outputs to non-sensitive datasets
Review validation-result retention settings
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl has broad network egress and supports multiple instances; Great Expectations can install packages but has no network egress. They do not show overlapping write scopes, shared mutable resources, or git/database access, so direct capability conflict is limited unless an external orchestrator gives them the same writable target.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator assigns both agents write access to the same directory or repository
IF package installation by Great Expectations mutates a shared environment used by Firecrawl
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Pin dependencies in a dedicated environment
Run one agent at a time for shared resources
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces scraped content and structured data that Great Expectations can plausibly consume for validation. If Great Expectations treats Firecrawl output as authoritative without verification, bad scrape data can cascade into incorrect validation results or downstream decisions. Great Expectations is a checker, but the handoff still creates a default pipeline risk.
conditions: IF Great Expectations consumes Firecrawl output without schema or source verification
IF validation results are used downstream as if they certify the scraped data
mitigations: Validate Firecrawl outputs against a schema before ingestion
Mark scraped data as untrusted in Great Expectations configs
Add a human review gate for failed or borderline validations
Keep validation results separate from source data
requires-engineering: add source-authenticity checks

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl handles API keys and scraped web content, while Great Expectations handles data-quality artifacts and documentation. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, so compliance risk is limited to generic handling differences rather than a specific breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is scraped by Firecrawl and then stored in Great Expectations artifacts
IF retention policies for validation results differ from source-data retention
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows
Set short retention for validation artifacts
Document data-class handling for both agents
Review logs for sensitive fields
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
